A regression test (or the existing suite) proves no-flag invocation is unchanged; the #267 escape-refusal test still passes against the evidence root.

intent.goal: Let one verify.py invocation reach two authorities — evidence paths bounded under one root, SHA/git legs run against another — and close round 2's Required findings without widening that change: the legacy no-flag path keeps its 20s symbol-grep budget (S2-R3), the root classifier and the canonical bound are pinned by tests that a mutant cannot walk past (R2-T1/T2/T3), and the fail-closed branch is covered rather than waived (H-7).
intent.ruled_out: A named _LEGACY_GREP_TIMEOUT constant for the restored budget: verify.py's interface WIDTH is a ratchet with two slots left before the pre-deepening baseline, and a timeout is not an interface. The value is passed at the call site and pinned by a test that reads it off the subprocess call and compares it to _run's own default, so it cannot drift back to _git's 10s unnoticed. Also ruled out: waiving the pragma at verify.py:209 — a branch nobody executes is a branch nobody knows the sign of, and the floor guard is right to say so.
intent.why: Round 2 was NO-GO on evidence discipline, one real compatibility regression and four coverage gaps; a round-3 NO-GO parks the unit. The compatibility regression is the one that mattered: it fired with both new flags ABSENT, which is the invocation the unit promised to leave byte-identical.

negative_control.did: checked out head_sha cd07307e in a throwaway worktree and ran the unit's class GREEN (27 tests, exit 0, nc-green.txt); then restored runtime/scripts/verify.py from base_sha a58bf71a (git checkout a58bf71a -- runtime/scripts/verify.py), left the round-3 tests in place, and re-ran: exit 1, 24 assertion failures and 1 error (nc-red.txt). The single error is honest and expected of a BASE revert rather than a behavioural mutant: at base there is no _ROOTS at all, so the round-3 fail-closed-classifier test cannot even reach an assertion.
